The *Alignment Journal* is now open to submissions from everyone. I’m part of the team behind it.

It’s a free-to-read, free-to-publish journal for research on the scientific foundations of understanding, predicting and steering AI systems. It welcomes work that builds theoretical or otherwise principled analyses, and whose significance survives the deletion of any particular model, dataset or benchmark. Empirical investigations of such ideas are welcome, and negative results are encouraged. Of particular interest are approaches that could apply to future superintelligent systems that interact and self-improve.

What the Journal does differently:
• Every accepted paper is published with a “review summary” to retain insights generated during the review.
• Reviewers are paid, with bonuses for speed and insight.
• Each paper is judged against the Journal’s acceptance bar, not against other submissions.
• Papers under review are listed publicly, so researchers can nominate themselves to review one.
If you have work that falls within the <https://www.alignmentjournal.org/open/policies/scope-and-acceptance-criteria|Journal’s scope>, consider <https://www.alignmentjournal.org/submissions/new|submitting>. If you want to review or act as an action editor, create an account for that at our <https://www.alignmentjournal.org/|website>.

Read more about the Alignment Journal's approach: <https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/xGucXHQ3NLkHZL3Cg>

:rocket: *Beijing AI Safety Residency: now recruiting for Spring 2027*
Managing frontier risks like loss of control will require international coordination — including with China, a fast follower on frontier AI. We're opening applications for the second cohort of a three-month residency for AI safety researchers to live and work alongside Chinese researchers at a <https://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/info/1177/127464.htm|new AI safety hub in Beijing>, affiliated with Tsinghua University, China’s top S&T university. The hub is co-directed by Xu Wei and <https://sorenmindermann.substack.com/p/why-im-becoming-a-professor-in-ai|Sören Mindermann>, with Andrew Yao as Chief Scientist.

*What it is:* A self-directed residency. You bring your own research agenda, and you get community and access to safety researchers at Chinese universities and labs.

*Who it's for:* Technical AI safety researchers (alignment, evals, oversight, control) with 1–3 publications or similar. No Mandarin or China background needed. Researchers with technical governance/governance backgrounds should also feel free to apply, though there are fewer spots for governance.

*Support:* $5k/month, plus flights, housing, visa support, and devices.

*We’re accepting applications for the seventh iteration of the AI Security Bootcamp, our second in San Francisco!*
<https://aisb.dev|AI Security Bootcamp> is a fully funded program for senior security professionals shaping how we secure frontier AI systems.

AISB is a 7-day intensive focused on the real risks as frontier AI systems become more capable and are targeted by sophisticated attackers. The program covers threat modeling, adversarial attacks, LLM security, infrastructure controls, weight security, formal verification, data center security, and AI control and hardware governance. It runs January 10-16, 2027 in San Francisco.

We are looking for security professionals with 5+ years of hands-on experience. No AI or ML background required. Past participants have been affiliated with OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Apple, AWS, CoreWeave, Palo Alto Networks, Snyk, Apollo Research, MIT, Stanford, Oxford and national security agencies.

Applications close *November 7th (AoE)*. <https://airtable.com/appyq1bBRnK6s7AkM/paglvXzxYAiJclCZX/form|Apply here>, or learn more at <http://aisb.dev/sf27|aisb.dev/sf27>

If you know someone who might be a strong candidate, please share this with them, or send them this <https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7517943750099234817|linkedin post>

Your **AI Safety** perspective belongs in public service. (*my emphasis*)

<https://matsprogram.org/|MATS> runs an AI safety research fellowship. We're looking for a contractor to build a new assessment for applicants to our empirical research track, and we’re offering bounties:
• *$200* if you refer someone and we invite them to our paid trial task.
• *$1,000* if someone you referred builds an assessment we actually give to applicants.
Candidates need to have empirical AI safety research experience - it's also beneficial if they have experience designing technical assessments.

To refer someone, dm me with the person's name and contact details, two or three sentences on why they fit, and links to their research and anything they've built. Please check with them before putting them forward. Note that if you’re reading this you’re welcome to apply but we don’t allow self-referrals.

If we’re interested in working with them, we’ll invite them to a short call, then a paid work test, before making a decision.

You can find more information on what we want from the test here: <https://app.notion.com/p/matsprogram/MATS-Empirical-Work-Test-Bounty-3fda0e14b0ad80ef9ab5f421a156d270?source=copy_link|app.notion.com/p/matsprogram/MATS-Empiric…?source=copy_link>

Propensity Labs is hiring for a pretty senior role:

> *Founding Engineer, Propensity Labs (SF, in person)*
> 
> Every model behaves differently and needs to be used differently. As AI takes on more of the economy, we believe a new layer will emerge that understands and steers model behavior. We’re building this layer - a compiler between human intent and the models underneath. This is our vision: <https://www.propensitylabs.ai/vision|propensitylabs.ai/vision>
> 
> Rahul, our CEO, is a former senior staff engineer at Meta and AWS with 12+ years of experience. Mana (myself), co-founder and Chief Scientist, an Information Systems professor who ran an academic research lab, and before that led a data infrastructure team at DoorDash. We’ve spent the last 1.5 years studying AI behavior, have published on it, and are now building a comprehensive taxonomy of AI misbehaviors and how to steer models away from them. We're backed by South Park Common (the same folks who incubated Goodfire), are partnering on research with a lab, and are iterating on our first product.
> 
> You’ll be our founding engineer and own infrastructure and production. You'll build the product and make the technical calls along with us. You'll set the engineering bar for everyone who joins after you.
> Required
> • 5+ years as an engineer, including owning a production system with real users end to end and being on call for it. Personal projects, hackathons, and demos don’t count toward this.
> • You’ve built a v1 from scratch with a vague spec and shipped it to customers.
> • You’ve built on frontier models in a real product, not just tutorials or wrappers.
> • You have deployed and operated containerized systems in the cloud.
> • You use AI coding tools heavily every day and ship experiments in days, not weeks.
> • You make technical calls without supervision and push back when you disagree.
> • You’ve already acted on your concern about AI alignment: work, projects, research, or writing you can point to.
> • You're able to and comfortable moving and iterating very fast.
> *Bonus:* evals or agent harnesses, early-stage startup experience, public technical work.
> 
> To apply, fill out <https://www.propensitylabs.ai/founding-engineer-2098a7|this form> with:
> • Your LinkedIn profile
> • A link to something you built that real users depended on, and your role in it
> • In under 150 words: why AI alignment, and what you’ve done about it so far. Please write this yourself; we want to see how you think.
> We read every complete application.
> We are not able to sponsor visa applications, unfortunately.
